project.title: Measure clock timing and gate delay
project.question: How do clock timing and propagation delay appear in preserved logic events?
project.notes:
Expected: Rising-edge delay from Clock to After 20 ns is 20 ns. Complete clock cycles are 100 ns, 10 MHz and 25% duty. High pulses are 25 ns. The final cycle is incomplete at the run boundary.
Try: Measure falling-to-falling delay, then change the second buffer delay to 20n and compare the saved measurements from both revisions.
assumptions: Native 0/1/X/Z event logic with transport delays and 1 ps timing; initial combinational settling does not create a clock edge.
No drive strengths, setup/hold timing, physical metastability, or supply-current model.

annotations.text: Run, then choose Timing to measure the saved edge pairs.

engine.name: CircuitBench event logic
engine.execution: JavaScript · isolated Web Worker · fresh instance per run
engine.initialization: Combinational logic settles at time zero; flip-flops, registers and counters use their explicit initial state.
engine.simultaneousInputs: All driver changes at one timestamp resolve together. Rising-edge state elements sample the resulting inputs; register and counter words update atomically.
engine.sequentialControls: Register/counter reset and enable are synchronous and active high; reset wins. Ambiguous edges or controls retain only bit values common to every possible outcome.
engine.limitations: No setup/hold, metastability, drive strengths, HDL, or analog feedback coupling.

result.pairing: For each source edge, use the first selected target edge at or after it and strictly before the next selected source edge. A target is never reused. Equal timestamps give zero delay. This temporal pairing does not establish physical causation.
